narrative: Material PL2__ME884243 shows intermittent, heavy-tailed demand (CV=1.406, 46.2% non-zero days) with highly variable supplier lead times (CV=0.666, range 0.18–3.12 days). The SAP baseline carries zero safety stock, leaving the operation effectively unprotected against demand and lead-time variability. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy with a safety stock of 5,068 units and EOQ-based order quantity of 11,353 units is recommended, achieving a 95% service level at an 8.8% lower total annual cost than the MOQ-only baseline.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The intermittent but large-batch demand pattern and variable lead times favour a continuous-review trigger policy; the fixed EOQ-based order quantity minimises total inventory costs while the reorder point absorbs both demand and lead-time uncertainty.
research_insights.boundary_risk: None — recommended policy uses 46.8% of storage capacity; no capacity constraint is binding and MOQ is comfortably below EOQ.
